title: Incident triage snapshot collector for PagerDuty/Slack
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight microservice that automatically attaches a diagnostic snapshot to PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads. The snapshot should include: 1) a small set of prioritized trace spans (service entry, hot handler, and error spans), 2) metric windows (p95/p99, error rate, throughput) for the 5m/30m/1h windows around the alert, 3) the top 3 log excerpts correlated to the trace IDs, 4) a suggested runbook snippet and remediation commands derived from the owning service's runbook metadata and SLO guardrails. Goal is to speed time-to-detect root-cause for oncall engineers and reduce mean-time-to-triage by surfacing focused evidence and action items.
acceptance_criteria: For any PagerDuty incident created by our alerts pipeline, an HTTP call to the snapshot service must attach a compact markdown snapshot to the PD incident with trace spans, metric windows, and log excerpts.
For Slack alert channels where the Ops bot is present, the service posts a thread reply with the same snapshot and buttons for 'Create Postmortem Draft' and 'Attach Runbook'.
Snapshot generation must complete in < 3s for incidents triggered by production SLO alerts under normal load (median).
Runbook snippet includes a primary remediation step + safe rollback commands and links to the owning service's full runbook in Confluence.
Automated postmortem draft includes the snapshot as evidence when triggered by a PD incident of severity >= 2.
End-to-end tests that mock traces/metrics/logs validate correct sectioning and that attachments are created with valid PD and Slack IDs.
design_notes: Service is pull-model: on PD incident creation a lightweight incident webhook will send minimal context (service, alert_rule, incident_id). Snapshot service will then fetch traces/metrics/logs using a bounded query window to avoid heavy queries during SLO spikes.

Trace selection heuristics: prefer spans with error tags, high duration relative to p95 for that endpoint, and spans that include voluminous logs. If none found, return top three spans by cumulative duration.
Metric windows will be computed from pre-aggregated TSDB rollups to keep query latency low (we'll use existing metrics-query API with new 'incident-window' aggregation parameter).

Runbook snippets will be stored as YAML frontmatter on each service's runbook page and indexed in a small metadata table keyed by service and alert_rule. We'll include semantic tags for remediation type (restart, scale, config, network).
Security: snapshots will avoid including any raw PII or full log bodies; log excerpts must be sanitized according to our PII-redaction policy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + fetcher (1 week) — implement incident webhook handler, bounded fetch routines for traces/metrics/logs, and snapshot formatter.
Phase 2: PD + Slack integration (1 week) — attach PD note via API, Slack thread post with interactive buttons, permissioned bot token usage.
Phase 3: Runbook integration & SLO hints (1 week) — index runbook snippets, implement simple SLO-based remediation ranking.
Phase 4: Tests & staging rollout (1 week) — integration tests, chaos scenarios (high alert storms), performance tuning, observability for snapshot service itself.
Phase 5: Gradual rollout to teams (2 weeks) — enable opt-in for 10 services, gather feedback, iterate on snippet wording and span-selection heuristics.
tests: Unit tests for span selection heuristics with synthetic trace bundles.
Integration test that simulates a PagerDuty webhook and verifies PD note and Slack thread creation in staging.
Load test: generate 200 alert webhooks/minute and assert median snapshot generation < 3s and tail < 6s.
Security tests validating log redaction and that no secret artifacts are included in attachments.
rollback_plan: Feature flag gated rollout. If snapshot service causes >1% increase in alert handling latency or any PD API errors >0.5% of calls in 15m window, flip feature flag off and auto-cleanup in-flight attachments via companion job.
